title: Carney, Cuddy & Yap (2010): Power posing
materials: original article: journal full text consulted to verify reported statistics; replication/p-curve/commentary literature: excerpts of the primary texts obtained via search; first author's 2016 statement: excerpts
decision_context: whether to rely on power posing as a low-cost intervention for confidence in high-stakes situations

claims.evidence_location: Results, felt-power analysis (verified against journal full text)
claims.falsifiers: null felt-power effect at adequate power; negative direction vs neutral control
claims.label: OBSERVED

claims.evidence_location: Results, risk-tolerance analysis (verified against journal full text)

claims.label: OBSERVED

claims.label: OBSERVED

claims.evidence_location: Results, hormone analyses (verified against journal full text)

claims.label: OBSERVED

tools.output: routed EMPIRICAL (defaults; no overrides needed); design checks recorded separately above

4 claims extracted, statistics verified against journal full text. Conditional rigidity (assessor-authored formalization of the public retelling): original formalized as IF [participants adopt expansive poses] THEN ([felt power rises] AND [risk tolerance rises] AND [testosterone rises] AND [cortisol falls]); antecedent-loss comparison (IF [pose] THEN [risk rises] vs bare [risk rises]) returns ASSERTED_CONSEQUENT (operator dropped: premise deleted, consequent stated as unconditional fact); retelling A (single conjunct) and retelling B (TED-style life outcomes) both NOT_ENTAILED - logically incomparable, neither entails the other; retelling B adds a new atom no original conjunct covers. Falsifiers for hormone/risk claims: null effects at adequate power - reported by Ranehill 2015 and Ronay 2016.
tools.source: vendored/conditional_claims.py run outputs; Slate 2016 for TED phrasing

tools.output: layer findings: testosterone layer instrument CONTAMINATED (gambling win feedback before saliva sampling; admitted in 2016 statement); felt-power self-report layer: many questions asked, chosen subset reported -> MEASURED_DISCARDED with discard rule undeclared at publication (disclosed 2016); exclusions: 5 of 47 -> MEASURED_DISCARDED, discard rule undeclared; join check Carney2010 vs Ranehill2015 on felt power: COMMENSURABLE as far as recorded excerpts show.
tools.source: 2016 statement excerpts; journal full text (no exclusions mentioned there)

tools.output: false_agree (false_agree.json): Ranehill2015~Cuddy2018-pcurve -> FALSE_AGREE_DEFINITION - a FIELD MISMATCH REQUIRING REVIEW, not a verdict: control structure and outcome scope differ (per commentary on Cuddy et al. 2018); assessor judges the control-structure difference load-bearing for the expansive-vs-neutral question. safe_provenance on data lineage (provenance-data.json): all pairs NO_SHARED_ANCESTOR_IN_DECLARED_GRAPH - property of the declared graph only. safe_provenance on methods lineage (provenance-methods.json): SOME_PAIRS_SHARE_ANCESTORS (witness: Carney 2010 methods); what the shared node contributes is study-specific: Ronay 2016 states exact replication of Carney et al. methodology; for Ranehill 2015 and Garrison 2016 inheritance of specific design features is NOT established from the excerpts in hand.

open branches for the felt-power effect: (a) expansive pose raises felt power; (b) contractive pose lowers it (difference is harm-driven); (c) demand/expectation effect; (d) publication bias artifact. Cheapest discriminators: neutral-pose control (b), blinded participants/experimenters (c), preregistered studies (d). (d) partially eliminated: Gronau et al. 2017 Bayesian meta-analysis of preregistered studies found a small positive effect on felt power (per Clearer Thinking summary). (a) vs (b): NOT ASSESSED - the exact pose/control contrasts in the cited studies (Ceunen et al. 2014; Garrison et al. 2016) were not verified from the primary texts in hand, and the commentary's argument that control-group designs favor (b) is the commentary authors' inference, not an independently verified finding here; the discrimination between (a) and (b) requires reading those designs and remains open. (c) remains open. Branches (a),(b),(c) remain open; no elimination completed by this assessment.
tools.source: commentary on Cuddy et al. 2018 (open.lnu.se); Clearer Thinking summary of Gronau et al. 2017

tools.output: claim-scope narrowing: defended claim family moved from 'neuroendocrine and behavioral changes' (2010) to 'feelings, emotions, affect' (2018 p-curve reply) to 'postural feedback' - recorded as REFERENT_NARROWED, an honest narrowing IF labeled as such; illicit drift only where the 2010 hormone/risk claims are still cited as supported - citation frequency not verified by this assessment. observer position: NOT_APPLICABLE. grounding layers: NOT_APPLICABLE. assumed stabilities: experimenter non-blindness (ASSUMED harmless at publication; unassessed then), gambling-win feedback independence (ASSESSED in 2016 statement: not stable, confound admitted).

labels: C1-C4 OBSERVED as reported statistics (verified); the abstract-level 'confirmed our prediction' framing is DERIVED from four separate tests; public retellings asserting life-outcome benefits are PROPOSED with no observation in the record. target vs rendering: the 2010 rendering is superseded; the target (do postures change felt states) remains open and partly answered. DECLINED: none - all cards read.

decisions.text: Rely on power posing as a confidence intervention before high-stakes situations?
Treat the 2010 hormone and risk-tolerance claims as established?
decisions.answer: No: UNSUPPORTED by direct replications at adequate power (Ranehill 2015: no effect on hormones or risk tolerance, N=200; Ronay 2016: no effect on testosterone, cortisol, risk, or felt power, exact method) and by p-curve analysis (Simmons & Simonsohn 2017); first author disavows the embodied-effects claim (2016 statement)

decisions.text: Spend research resources searching for moderators of the hormone/risk effects?
decisions.deferred_reason: Simmons & Simonsohn 2017: existing evidence too fragile to justify moderator search; re-open only with preregistered adequately-powered designs

design_checks.finding: gambling win feedback precedes saliva sampling; winning alone can raise testosterone (admitted as possible confound in first author's 2016 statement)
47 run, 5 excluded on bases like 'didn't follow directions'; exclusions not mentioned in the article
